messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert - elevated error-rate and latency for dedicated pool 'd-nyc-3' (tenant=acme) - paging oncall.
alex_m: oncall here, looking.
maya: seeing spikes on Grafana around 04:12 UTC; token failures and 500s.
tom_devops: on it. any customer reports?
lina_cs: AcmeCorp support called via SSO alert; they report some inference 500s and long-tail latency during morning traffic. They're on a quick bridge.
sarah_eng: quick metric scan: tenant 'acme' KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapsed from ~86% -> ~3% within ~10m. Backend model error count increased. GPU CPU on pool looks fine. Likely cache layer problem.
dmitri_research: could be prefix application bug or namespace collision; saw similar when prefix was omitted after a rollout.
alex_m: maya, pull kv-proxy logs for tenant=acme from d-nyc-3 and grep for prefix_applied.
maya: pulling logs now. snippet:
```
kv-proxy[pid=3124] INFO apply-prefix tenant_id=acme prefix=\"acme:\" enabled=true config_hash=0x7a2
kv-proxy[pid=3128] WARN cache-miss key=\"user_prompt\" tenant_id=acme prefix_applied=false
kv-proxy[pid=3130] ERROR store-write failed key=\"acme:prompt:xyz\" err=EACCES
```
maya: lots of prefix_applied=false and some EACCES on store writes.
tom_devops: EACCES suggests ACL/permission issue against Redis in the VPC or credential mismatch after key rotation.
lina_cs: customer mentioned they rotated KMS keys earlier today.
sarah_eng: EACCES would prevent writes, so cache population stops, hit-rate collapses -> more direct model calls -> more latency and some timeouts.
alex_m: immediate mitigation steps: 1) disable KV cache reads/writes for tenant acme via feature-flag to stop failing writes and global pollution; 2) run diagnostics and list keys for acme prefix; 3) targeted flush of acme:* keys if safe; 4) route acme traffic to fallback model to reduce load; 5) infra to fix redis ACLs/creds.
maya: toggling feature-flag acme.kv_cache.enabled=false on pool d-nyc-3 now.
deploy-bot: feature-flag acme.kv_cache.enabled=false applied to pool d-nyc-3 by maya.
maya: reads/writes should be bypassed.
sarah_eng: applying routing policy to fallback model redwood-small-fallback and lower concurrency (20rps) for acme.
alex_m: routing change applied, draining old model.
tom_devops: checking redis ACLs in VPC - it shows denied write for our service account. I can provision a temporary service user but need ops approval for credential rotation.
dmitri_research: recommend targeted deletion rather than global flush while infra fixes creds. Example on bastion:
```
redis-cli -h redis.vpc.internal --scan --pattern \"acme:*\" | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis.vpc.internal del
```
maya: running scan (dry-run) to count keys.
maya: found ~12,039 keys. lina_cs, confirm deletion with customer?
lina_cs: AcmeCorp said stale cache is fine as long as service returns to normal quickly; they approve targeted flush.

alex_m: tom_devops to coordinate creds.
tom_devops: creds rotation approved; creating temporary service user now.
deploy-bot: temporary service user for redis-access-service created (expires 12h).
tom_devops: running targeted delete on bastion using temp credentials:
```
redis-cli -h redis.vpc.internal -a $TEMP_PASS --scan --pattern \"acme:*\" | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis.vpc.internal -a $TEMP_PASS del
```
maya: delete finished - 12,039 keys removed.
sarah_eng: prepare to re-enable cache but gate it: maya toggle acme.kv_cache.enabled=true for a short test window and watch write-errors.
maya: toggling true for 60s test window.
maria_monitor-bot: kv-proxy metrics (tenant=acme): write-errors -> 0 after deletion; cache-population ~200 rps; hit-rate warming from 0% -> 12%.
alex_m: good. leave enabled but add circuit-breaker: if write-errors > 5 within 1m auto-disable cache for tenant.
deploy-bot: circuit-breaker rule added for tenant=acme.
lina_cs: customer updated on call; errors cleared, they see slower responses initially while cache warms, they accept.
sarah_eng: initial postmortem notes: root cause likely ACL misconfiguration after KMS rotation combined with a bug where prefix_applied=false allowed writes to skip prefix causing cache pollution; impact: tenant-level hit-rate collapse -> increased latency and 500s. Mitigations: feature-flag disable, targeted key flush, temp creds, fallback model routing, circuit-breaker.
alex_m: follow-ups assigned: eng-runtime add guard to assert prefix_applied==true or fail-safe (owner: sarah_eng); infra to investigate KMS rotation effects on redis ACLs (owner: tom_devops); cs to coordinate customer timeline and postmortem (owner: lina_cs); ops to create automated targeted-flush runbook (owner: maya).
maria_monitor-bot: incident duration 00:42 so far; error-rate trending back to baseline.
lina_cs: created incident ticket INC-2026-2247 per customer request.
alex_m: handing off to follow-up owners; I'll stay on the postmortem. tagging @sarah_eng @tom_devops @lina_cs @maya.
sarah_eng: ack - will draft postmortem.
tom_devops: ack - will deep-dive redis ACLs and KMS rotation logs.
maya: ack - will add targeted-flush playbook to runbook with safe commands and dry-run steps.
lina_cs: ack - will send customer summary and next steps.
incident-bot: monitoring for 1h stabilization; incident resolved? false.
alex_m: marking thread for follow-up; closing on-call shift in 30m.
